meta.title: Top 20 World Container Ports
meta.source: World Shipping Council / AAPA / Port Authorities

items.name: Port of Shanghai
items.summary: The world's busiest container port since 2010. Located at the mouth of the Yangtze River, including the automated Yangshan Deep Water Port connected via the 32.5km Donghai Bridge.

items.name: Port of Singapore
items.summary: The principal global transshipment hub connecting Asia, Europe, and the Americas across the Malacca & Singapore Straits, currently expanding into Tuas Mega Port.
items.sourceLabel: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore

items.name: Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan
items.summary: Handles the world's largest total cargo tonnage, serving China's manufacturing heartland in Zhejiang province with deep-water berths across Zhoushan archipelago.
items.keyExports: Textiles, Heavy Machinery, Plastics, Chemical Products

items.name: Port of Shenzhen
items.summary: Comprising Yantian, Chiwan, and Shekou terminals in the Pearl River Delta. Serves southern China's global technology and electronics manufacturing clusters.

items.name: Port of Qingdao
items.summary: A major hub on the Yellow Sea operating fully automated container terminals, handling crude oil, iron ore, and international container trade with North Asia.
items.keyExports: Heavy Industry, Tires, Appliance Goods, Agricultural Exports

items.name: Port of Guangzhou
items.summary: The main economic and maritime gateway for Guangdong province, centered at Nansha Deepwater Port, connecting domestic river trade with ocean container lines.

items.name: Port of Busan
items.summary: South Korea's dominant port handling ~75% of national container traffic and serving as a crucial feeder and transshipment hub for Japan, Russia, and China.

items.name: Port of Tianjin
items.summary: The largest artificial port in Northern China, serving as the main sea gateway to Beijing and Tianjin metropolitan areas and the Bohai Economic Rim.
items.keyExports: Steel Products, Heavy Machinery, Manufactured Goods

items.name: Port of Hong Kong
items.summary: A world-famous natural deep-water harbour featuring Kwai Tsing Container Terminals, historically driving Asia-Pacific trade and South China transshipment.
items.sourceLabel: Hong Kong Maritime and Port Board

items.name: Port of Rotterdam
items.summary: Europe's largest port stretching 40km from the city center to Maasvlakte 2 on the North Sea. Serves as the primary logistics gateway to Germany and Western Europe.

items.name: Port Klang
items.summary: Malaysia's main maritime gateway located 38km southwest of Kuala Lumpur on the Strait of Malacca, comprised of Northport and Westport container facilities.
items.keyExports: Palm Oil, Electronics, Rubber Products, Chemicals

items.name: Port of Antwerp-Bruges
items.summary: Europe's second-largest port following the 2022 merger of Antwerp and Zeebrugge. Located on the Scheldt estuary with extensive inland European barge and rail links.

items.name: Jebel Ali / Dubai Port
items.summary: Operated by DP World, Jebel Ali is the largest man-made harbor in the world and the busiest port in the Middle East, serving the Persian Gulf and East Africa.

items.name: Port of Los Angeles
items.summary: North America's leading seaport by container volume, occupying 7,500 acres along San Pedro Bay and handling major transpacific ocean trade with Asia.
items.keyExports: Agricultural Produce, Waste Paper, Chemicals, Machinery

items.name: Port of Long Beach
items.summary: Adjoining the Port of Los Angeles in San Pedro Bay, Long Beach is a major US gateway for Transpacific trade with green port initiatives and high-volume rail corridors.

items.name: Tanger Med Port
items.summary: Located on the Strait of Gibraltar, Tanger Med has rapidly grown into the largest container port in the Mediterranean and Africa, connected to 180 global ports.

items.name: Port of Colombo
items.summary: Strategically positioned on the main East-West Indian Ocean shipping lane, handling over 70% of transshipment cargo for India and the South Asian subcontinent.

items.name: Port of Hamburg
items.summary: Located on the River Elbe 110km from the North Sea, Hamburg is Germany's largest seaport and the primary rail freight hub connecting Central and Eastern Europe.
items.keyExports: Machinery, Automotive Parts, Chemical Goods, Metals

items.name: Port of Kaohsiung
items.summary: Taiwan's largest harbor handling over 65% of the island's container traffic, equipped with 5 container terminals serving major East Asian sea lanes.

items.name: Port of Santos
items.summary: Latin America's busiest container port located in São Paulo state, handling over 28% of Brazil's total foreign trade exchange.
items.keyExports: Coffee, Soybeans, Sugar, Iron Ore, Meat Products
